segments.title: HMAS Geranium's rapid 1915 build
segments.summary: HMAS Geranium was an Arabis-class sloop laid down in August and launched on 8 November 1915, only a few months later.
segments.body: HMAS Geranium was an Arabis-class sloop built in Scotland during the First World War. Her keel was laid in August 1915, and she was launched on 8 November. Only a few months separated laying down and launch, illustrating the speed of her wartime construction.

evidence.note: The transcript identifies Geranium's class, Scottish construction, August 1915 laying down, and 8 November launch.

segments.title: From Royal Navy sloop to Australian hulk
segments.summary: Geranium transferred to Australia in 1919, served until 1927, and was dismantled before her hulk was sunk in 1935.
segments.body: Geranium transferred from Royal Navy service to Australia in 1919. Her Australian service continued until she was decommissioned in 1927. Disposal took several more years: she was dismantled in 1932, and the remaining hulk was sunk in 1935.

evidence.note: The transcript dates Geranium's Australian transfer, decommissioning, dismantling, and sinking as a hulk.

segments.title: Range and coal in a 1,250-ton sloop
segments.summary: At 1,250 tons, Geranium could make 16.5 knots and cover about 2,000 nautical miles at 15 knots on 250 tons of coal.
segments.body: Geranium displaced 1,250 tons and measured 267 feet 9 inches in overall length. Her beam was 33 feet 6 inches and her draft 11 feet 9 inches. She carried 250 tons of coal and could cover about 2,000 nautical miles at 15 knots. Her top speed was 16.5 knots.

evidence.note: The transcript lists displacement, dimensions, speed, range, and the 250-ton coal load.

segments.title: Geranium's larger Australian crew and gun fit
segments.summary: Geranium's complement rose from 77 to 113, partly because the Royal Australian Navy used transferred ships to expand. Her armament included 4-inch guns later replaced by 4.7-inch guns.
segments.body: Geranium carried 77 personnel in Royal Navy service and 113 after transfer to the Royal Australian Navy. The use of transferred ships to expand the Australian service partly accounts for the larger complement. Her gun fit included two quick-firing 4-inch Mark IV guns in single mounts. These were later replaced by 4.7-inch Mark IV guns, and she also had two 3-pounders.

evidence.note: The transcript contrasts the two complements, partly attributes the increase to RAN expansion, and describes the gun fit through the two 3-pounders.

segments.title: Converting Geranium for hydrographic survey
segments.summary: Converted from an armed sloop, Geranium became the Royal Australian Navy's first survey vessel and later carried a Fairey III seaplane.
segments.body: Geranium entered the Royal Australian Navy as its first survey vessel. Her weapons were removed and survey equipment was fitted in their place. The sloop's design suited the installation of that equipment. She also carried a Fairey III seaplane.

evidence.note: The transcript identifies the Fairey III, the removal of weapons, survey equipment, and Geranium's first-survey-vessel role.

segments.title: A North Sea design in tropical survey waters
segments.summary: Geranium's Australian survey service brought tropical operating problems and repeated groundings, including one on an uncharted reef.
segments.body: Geranium was designed for a North Sea climate. She did not work well in the tropical waters where she served as a survey vessel. She also ran aground repeatedly, including on an uncharted reef off Vanderlin Island. Another grounding took place in the McArthur River.

evidence.note: The transcript links tropical operating difficulties to the North Sea design and names the grounding examples.

segments.title: Geranium assists the stranded Tasman
segments.summary: After being fitted to carry a Fairey III in 1924, Geranium assisted the steamship Tasman following a grounding off Clark Island.
segments.body: Geranium was fitted to carry a Fairey III seaplane in 1924. She subsequently assisted the steamship Tasman after it struck a reef off Clark Island. The details of that assistance, including any role for the seaplane, are not specified.

evidence.note: The transcript says Geranium was fitted for a Fairey III in 1924 and assisted Tasman after the latter hit a reef off Clark Island.
